title: The Margin Ledger
brief: Write a cosy mystery set in a small town lending library. Someone has been writing tiny dates in the margins of returned books. The librarian works out who and why. Fair-play clues; the answer is kind, not criminal.
worldBible: The town is Pellam Cross; the library is open Tuesday to Saturday only.
Books are stamped with a due date three weeks after borrowing.
The library has one photocopier and it has been broken for a year.
Every margin date is in pencil and precedes the book's stamped due date by exactly one day.
The library cat, Inkwell, sleeps on the returns trolley.

mustHold.fact: The margin dates are written in pencil.
mustHold.violationExample: The margin dates were written in blue ink.

mustHold.fact: The library is closed on Sundays and Mondays.
contradicts: \b(?:on (?:a )?(?:Sunday|Monday)|that (?:Sunday|Monday))\b[^.]{0,40}\b(?:opened the library|the library was open|unlocked the library)
mustHold.violationExample: On Monday morning Rosalind unlocked the library as usual.

mustHold.fact: The person writing the dates is Faraday Cole, reminding himself when books are due; no crime is involved.
mustHold.violationExample: Priya had been writing the dates all along, to cover a theft.

probes.question: Are the margin dates one day before the due date?
probes.passExample: Each pencilled date fell one day before the stamp.
probes.failExample: Each margin date was a week before the stamp.

probes.question: Is the cat still named Inkwell?
probes.passExample: Inkwell opened one eye on the returns trolley.

probes.question: Is Faraday identified as the writer?
probes.passExample: Faraday admitted he wrote the dates to remind himself.
